marks.gloss_en: לפי שאין עושין אותה אלא לגוון -- Yaakov Korcha's reason for the mishna's permission
Yaakov Korcha: because one makes it only for the colour
מאכל חמורים הוא ... אלא אמר שמואל: ממחו ביד -- Shmuel's ground for his own position
one may dissolve it by hand
שמע מינה -- from the stated teaching's adding amita (= mint) to cress, mint is good for cress
cress ground on Shabbat eve: on the morrow he may put oil and vinegar into it
mustard kneaded on Shabbat eve: on the morrow one may dissolve it with a vessel
Abaye and Rava: the halakha is not as R' Yochanan [who then permitted both]
Abaye and Rava: the halakha is as R' Yochanan [after he stood in R' Elazar's view]
Abaye's mother made it for him, and he did not eat
Mar Zutra: the halakha is not as any of these teachings
[the mishna, cited:] and one may make anumlin on Shabbat
והא מר עוקבא דשתי כל יומא? -- Mar Ukva drank it every day [without harm]
שאני מר עוקבא דדש ביה -- Mar Ukva is different, for he was accustomed to it
Rav Yosef: once I went in after Mar Ukva to the bathhouse; when I came out he gave me one cup of the wine, and I felt it from the hair of my head to the nail of my foot
one may not soak asafoetida in lukewarm water
one may not sift straw in a sieve
שלא יעשה כדרך שהוא עושה בחול -- Abaye's own reason
אלא מעתה שרה אומצא במיא הכי נמי דמיחייב? -- if soaking is liable, soaking meat in water would be liable too
Abaye's reductio: then one who soaked meat in water would also be liable? (asserted by no one)
אין שורין ... בפושרין -- הא בצונן מותר: an inference from the mishna's wording
והא אנן תנן: אין שורין את החלתית בפושרין -- הא בצונן מותר
[R' Yochanan asked: may one soak asafoetida in cold water?] R' Yannai: it is forbidden
דתניא ... רבי יוסי אומר: בחמין אסור, בצונן מותר -- the mishna's permission of cold water is R' Yosei's alone (bare דתניא: kind svara under protest)
דתניא: אין שורין את החלתית לא בחמין ולא בצונן -- the baraita's first clause forbids cold water, as R' Yannai ruled
אם כן מה בין לי ולך -- מתניתין יחידאה היא (= p_matnitin_yechidaa): the mishna is an individual's view, as the baraita shows
R' Yannai: the mishna is an individual's [view] -- R' Yosei's, per the baraita he cites
כיון דאישתי ... אי לא שתי בשבת מיסתכן
כמאן דשרי? -- is Rav's ruling per the one who permits [cold water], against the baraita's first clause which forbids?
אפילו למאן דאסר -- that applies only where he had not drunk at all; here, having drunk Thursday and Shabbat eve, he would be endangered (= p_issur_davka_lo_ishtei, p_taam_mistakken)
even per the one who forbids: that is only where he had not drunk at all
לרכוכי קא מיכוין -- Rav Safra's own reason
[Rav Acha asked Rav Safra: may one rub a linen shirt on Shabbat -- is it to soften, permitted, or to whiten, forbidden?] Rav Safra: he intends to soften, and it is permitted
ותיפשוט ליה למר מסודרא -- let the Master resolve the shirt from Rav Huna's ruling on the scarf
התם מיחזי כי אולודי חיורא, הכא לא מיחזי כאולודי חיורא -- the one looks like whitening and the other does not, so the scarf does not resolve the shirt
[dilemma: one who soaked (asafoetida), what?] Rav Adda of Naresh before Rav Yosef: one who soaked is liable to a sin-offering
what is it [soaked asafoetida] made for? for heaviness of the heart
[Rav Acha: my dilemma is soaking.] Rav Huna: thus says Rav -- one soaks [asafoetida] in cold water and puts it in the sun

Rav Acha: about a scarf I had no dilemma, for I asked Rav Huna and he resolved it for me [the text says only ופשט לי; permissive per 140a.23's proposed inference, and per the Rif as Steinsaltz cites him]
Rav Chisda: this linen shirt -- pulling it off the reed is permitted
